item.title: Tim Berners-Lee — Cool URIs don’t change
item.description: A small manifesto for permanent links: links as promises, not disposable plumbing.

item.title: John Allsopp — A Dao of Web Design
item.description: Responsive web thinking before “responsive design” had a name.

item.title: Rebecca Blood — Weblogs: A History and Perspective
item.description: It preserves human selection: someone found a thing, thought about it, and linked with voice.

item.title: Clay Shirky — A Group Is Its Own Worst Enemy
item.description: It reads like a field manual for every platform community failure that followed.

item.title: Joel Spolsky — The Law of Leaky Abstractions
item.description: A durable warning against smooth tools, black boxes, and fake simplicity.

item.title: Richard P. Gabriel — The Rise of Worse is Better
item.description: It explains half the software world with an uncomfortable little knife.

item.title: Calculated Risk — Housing: Speculation is the Key
item.description: Independent diagnosis from before the crash became obvious.

item.title: Warren Buffett — Mr. Buffett on the Stock Market
item.description: A calm valuation note written while the room was drunk.

item.title: Jo Freeman — The Tyranny of Structurelessness
item.description: Still one of the sharpest texts about organizations, communities, and informal control.

item.title: Bertrand Russell — In Praise of Idleness
item.description: Old enough to be public-domain furniture, sharp enough to cut modern work culture.
